title: HB418 (135th Legislature (2023-2024)): Regards carrying a concealed handgun, licensee's duties

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Ohio) (gun-policy Stage 5, Ohio); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Ohio text (As Introduced (00_IN), ; official copy, https://search-prod.lis.state.oh.us/api/v2/general_assembly_135/legislation/hb418/00_IN/pdf/ (Open States text id 90134053))
provenance.note: As introduced (135th GA); file is about 226k characters across 24 sections, so the quote is a selection from R.C. 2923.12 and the 2923.111 repeal; other sections (109.69, 109.731, 311.41-.43, 1547.69, 2921.13, 2923.11, 2923.121-.129, 2923.1210-.1213, 2923.16, 2953.35, 5502.411) mostly swap 'concealed handgun' for 'basic competency' licence wording. Struck in R.C. 2923.12: the 2022 text that dropped the duty to disclose to officers (replaced by the duty to inform), the carve-out for people already licensed, and the expungement paragraph (E)(2). Section 4 (uncodified) is a composite-section finding.

operative_text:
Section 3 (R.C. 2923.111): That section 2923.111 of the Revised Code is hereby repealed.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.12): (B)(1) If the person is stopped for a law enforcement purpose and is carrying a concealed handgun, fail to inform any law enforcement officer who approaches the person after the person has been stopped that the person has been issued a basic competency license and that the person then is carrying a concealed handgun,
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.12): (2) If the person is stopped for a law enforcement purpose and is carrying a concealed handgun, knowingly fail to keep the person's hands in plain sight at any time after any law enforcement officer begins approaching the person while stopped and before the law enforcement officer leaves, unless the failure is pursuant to and in accordance with directions given by a law enforcement officer;
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.12): (2) Division (A)(2) of this section does not apply to any person who, at the time of the alleged carrying or possession of a handgun, either is carrying a valid basic competency license or is an active duty member of the armed forces of the United States and is carrying a valid military identification card and documentation of successful completion of firearms training that meets or exceeds the training requirements described in division (G)(1) of section 2923.125 of the Revised Code, unless the person knowingly is in a place described in division (B) of section 2923.126 of the Revised Code.
Section 1 (R.C. 2923.12): (E) No person who is charged with a violation of this section shall be required to obtain a basic competency license as a condition for the dismissal of the charge.
